start.q: Is there an immediate threat to life or safety?

emergency.text: Call 911 for immediate danger or life-threatening symptoms. Do not ask volunteers to diagnose or manage emergencies alone.

firstaid.q: Can basic first aid reasonably address the concern?

aid.text: Offer appropriate first-aid resources within training and supplies. Reassess if symptoms worsen or the person wants further care.

timing.q: WHEN: Is this a prompt new concern or an ongoing issue?

acute.text: Consider urgent care or hospital based on urgency; confirm access. Ask what the person wants and whether they already have a provider.
opts: Continue: HOW will they get there?

ongoing.q: WHERE: Connect or reconnect with a provider
ongoing.text: Explore existing primary care and specialist access; do not assume Clinica is the only option.
opts: Continue: HOW will they get there?

transport.q: HOW: Can they get to the appointment?
transport.text: Consider walking, bus passes, accompaniment, or Medicaid NEMT for eligible appointments. BFF has experienced NEMT difficulties; confirm the ride.

advocacy.q: ADVOCACY: Would they like help navigating care?
advocacy.text: Ask permission before calling, scheduling, accompanying, or speaking for them. Volunteers may arrange a public-place follow-up; no promise of an advocate.

followup.text: Agree on a realistic next step, a contact method, and who will check back. For ongoing complexity, connect to a case manager.

prevention.text: Explore urgent rental assistance, benefits and employment support. Preserve existing housing if possible.

shelter.text: Check current access rules, pet needs, transport and alternatives; never promise a bed.

longterm.text: Connect to Coordinated Entry and a housing case manager, and explore independent pathways in parallel.

start.q: What kind of help does the person want?

jobs.text: Ask about prior experience, interests, and what is preventing a return to work.

training.text: Career development resources exist, including after housing. Help search without promising a particular program.

barriers.text: Ask which barrier matters to this person rather than assuming.

start.q: What kind of help is the person requesting?

crisis.text: 988 and emergency options. CIRT may involve police; CARE/non-police response cannot be promised. For immediate danger call 911.

outreach.text: WellMind/CAT is a possible resource; confirm current availability and whether they will meet outside.

therapy.text: A good fit may take several tries. Help search covered providers; do not pressure someone to remain with a provider they dislike.

start.q: What does the person want right now?

safer.text: Respect participant goals; offer safer-use resources without pressuring treatment.

treatment.text: Ask whether they want detox, residential, IOP or MAT. Confirm intake and transport before making promises.

peer.text: Offer peer support and follow-up if requested.

vital.title: Vital Documents: ID, Birth Certificate, Social Security Card

idcheck.q: Is someone already working on getting the ID?

bccheck.q: Is someone already working on the birth certificate?

sscheck.q: Is someone already working on the Social Security card?

already.text: Ask who is helping. With participant permission, contact that person or agency to learn what has happened and what comes next. Multiple birth certificate orders through different agencies can create problems.

idprior.q: Have you had a Colorado ID before?

replacement.text: A fingerprint-based replacement may be possible for a prior Colorado ID. An appointment is generally needed. Focus is BFF’s preferred referral; All Roads or BFF can help. Confirm DMV requirements for the individual.
opts: Why is the ID needed now?

firstid.text: A birth certificate and Affidavit of Identity may be part of the process, with additional DMV requirements such as address evidence. Sebastian and Trisha at Focus are registered DMV identity affiants and BFF contacts for this path. RNs explain the steps and connect to Focus rather than doing complex identity work themselves.
opts: Why is the ID needed now?

bc.text: Connect to Focus or another case manager to check eligibility, application requirements, fees and state of birth. First check that no one else has already applied.

ss.text: Connect to Focus, BFF or All Roads for help with Social Security replacement procedures and identity evidence. Confirm current SSA requirements; do not promise an outcome.

stalled.text: Ask what happened and who has been helping. Colorado DMV has an Exceptions Processing procedure for complex cases. Refer to a case manager (Focus preferred) rather than trying to solve a complicated identity dispute as a volunteer. Official information: https://dmv.colorado.gov/exceptions-processing-application-process

goal.q: Why was this document needed right now?
goal.text: Can the immediate goal be met another way while the document process continues? Ask the relevant provider about alternative identification or exception procedures for treatment, medical care, benefits, work or housing. Do not promise an exception. Agree who follows up.

start.q: Is someone already helping with this?

existing.text: With the person’s permission, ask which case manager or provider is involved, what has been tried, and what help they want next.

need.q: What does the person want help with?

access.text: Ask what would make the service usable; help with practical barriers or connect to a specialist. Do not assume diagnosis or eligibility.

benefits.text: Connect to a case manager or qualified benefits navigator; check for existing applications first.

housing.text: Ask about existing supports and specific accessibility needs. Imagine! may be relevant for developmental disability services; verify eligibility.

work.text: Ask what kind of work the person wants and what accommodations would help. Connect to specialized vocational services as appropriate.

advocacy.text: Identify the requested support and connect to a relevant specialist or case manager.

start.q: Does the person have the ticket or citation?

details.text: Read the court, date, deadline, citation number and instructions on the actual ticket. Do not guess deadlines or promise dismissal. Ask if a case manager or attorney is already involved.

missing.text: Connect to a case manager or legal navigator to identify the issuing agency and retrieve case information. Avoid guessing the court or deadline.

legal.text: With permission, help the person reach an appropriate legal aid or court-navigation contact. Preserve the citation and any paperwork.

housing.text: Ask what practical support is needed now, separately from the legal process.

opts: Taken during an enforcement or cleanup

official.text: Ask when and where it happened, which agency or crew was present, and whether a notice or receipt was provided. Do not promise items can be recovered.
opts: Need help locating or recovering belongings

unknown.text: Ask about the last known location and whether there is documentation. Refer to an advocate or case manager for next steps.

recover.q: Get assistance with the recovery process
recover.text: A case manager or legal advocate can help identify the appropriate agency, property process, and any applicable deadlines. Confirm current Boulder procedures before giving specific instructions.

replace.text: Prioritize medications, identification, weather protection and other immediate needs; coordinate with existing providers.
